danielle (customer): Hey, our app using EventSource to stream tokenized deltas is dropping mid-stream in Safari on iOS only. Partial output arrives then connection closes, works fine in Chrome and Firefox. Seen on customer org ID 8421, paid plan.

maria (support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal repro? Which URL, any proxy/CDN in front? Are you using cookies or auth headers?

danielle (customer): Using our CDN (FastEdge) + Redwood API behind it. We sign requests with Authorization header. Sample repro: user opens page, EventSource('/v1/stream?session=abc123') then after ~8-20s stream cuts with occasional 204/304 from CDN in dev tools. Happens on iOS 15 / Safari 16.

maria (support): Thanks. Can you capture response headers when it cuts? Even a screenshot of Network tab helps. Also is there any ServiceWorker in the page?

danielle (customer): Screenshot uploaded. Key headers: ``Content-Type: text/event-stream``, ``Transfer-Encoding: chunked``, ``Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000``, ``Vary: Accept-Encoding`` and sometimes CDN returns ``304 Not Modified`` on subsequent GETs. No service worker.

ashwin (eng): That Cache-Control + long max-age is suspect for SSE. If the CDN caches the SSE endpoint and later returns 304, Safari's EventSource/connection lifecycle can behave oddly and close the stream. Also CDNs often strip Authorization on cache hits, which breaks auth.

sam (devex): Repro steps we use internally: 1) curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://host/v1/stream?session=test" 2) open Safari on iOS with devtools proxy (or Charles) and observe chunked frames. Try toggling CDN by hitting origin host directly.

ashwin (eng): Workarounds: set SSE responses to not be cached by edge: ``Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0`` and add ``Vary: Authorization, Cookie`` so edge caches don't serve stale 304s for different auth. Also ensure CDN does not gzip or buffer chunks: ``Cache-Control: no-transform`` and disable compression for SSE content-type.

maria (support): Quick patch we can ask customer to test: add query param like `?sse_nocache=1` to bypass CDN caching OR set temporary origin header via host header. If they can't change CDN quickly, suggest switching to a signed query param instead of Authorization header (EventSource can't set custom headers).

ashwin (eng): Important server-side bits: always send a heartbeat (``: keep-alive\n\n``) every ~15s, keep `Connection: keep-alive`, Content-Type `text/event-stream; charset=utf-8`, and avoid ending response with an extra small trailing chunk that some browsers interpret as EOF. Also avoid returning 304 for SSE — if origin sees conditional GET it should return 200 with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

support-bot: Ticket created: #SUP-8421 assigned to eng-oncall.

eng-oncall: Picking this up. We'll check CDN config + origin behavior. Quick question: customer mentioned billing spikes — are they seeing repeated reconnects causing more tokens billed?

maria (support): Yes they reported bursts of reconnects inflating usage. They want a fast mitigation before eng change.

ashwin (eng): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Ask CDN admin to disable caching for `/v1/stream*` and set `Cache-Control: no-store` 2) Add `Vary: Authorization` and `Cache-Control: no-transform` at origin 3) Add server-side heartbeat to prevent midstream perceived EOF 4) Long-term: add explicit SSE endpoint exempt from CDN or use websocket.

sam (devex): I'll draft an email for the customer with exact headers and curl to test. Also add a snippet for customers using CloudFront / FastEdge: config block example below:

```
// origin response headers to set
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, max-age=0
Vary: Authorization, Cookie
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://your.origin.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
```

maria (support): Shared mitigation steps with customer and asked them to confirm after CDN rule change. Marking as escalated, assigning to eng-oncall for follow-up. :eyes:

danielle (customer): Thanks all — applying CDN rule now, will report back in ~10m. Appreciate the quick help. :pray:

eng-oncall: Noted. We'll monitor logs for spike pattern and run synthetic Safari tests against their origin and through FastEdge. If we see 304s coming back for SSE, we'll request a purge and block caching.

maria (support): Closing loop: once customer confirms stable stream we'll push a KB article describing SSE best-practices (no-cache endpoints, Vary header, no-transform, heartbeat).
